clue.text: Get rid of tea bag, going to pot filled by men the wrong way

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are filled, i.e. have something placed inside them
something gone to pot is ruined and in disorder, so the letters of tea bag are jumbled
men's abbreviation is read backwards, against the usual direction

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone throwing out a used tea bag while a clumsy team of men messes things up.
explanation.walkthrough: Men as other ranks is an army convention: ordinary soldiers as distinct from officers.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrogate a law or agreement is to repeal or abolish it, a formal synonym for doing away with it.

clue.text: Grab pastries, soft in the middle — a Scottish speciality

parts.note: to bag something is to grab or seize it

indicators.note: the soft letter is placed in the middle of the pastries word

parts.note: pies are pastries
P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: Someone snatching pastries with gooey centres, presented as a Scottish delicacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagpipes are the instrument most associated with Scotland, here whimsically called a national speciality.

clue.text: Managed love sonnets, perhaps, in French

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
sonnets are an example of verse
the French word for in is en

explanation.surface: Someone who managed love sonnets written in French, like a romantic literary editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee a project is to supervise or manage it.

clue.text: Detective attending houses in part of mine

indicators.note: the word for attending contains, or houses, the detective

parts.note: attending a function means being at it
DI is a Detective Inspector in the British police

explanation.surface: A police detective at the scene where some homes sit on land belonging to a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal entrance passage into a mine, one component of the workings.

clue.text: Joke in Seinfeld occasionally being used by someone else

indicators.note: the joke word goes inside the picked letters
taking only every other letter of Seinfeld, letters that appear now and then

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: A joke appearing in the sitcom Seinfeld now and then, borrowed by another comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' here takes the even-placed letters, not the odd ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone line or toilet that is engaged is occupied, already in use by another person.

clue.text: Conservative suffers defeat with experience near disaster

parts.note: someone who loses suffers a defeat
to have a bad time is to experience one

explanation.surface: A Conservative candidate loses the election and has a narrow brush with catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A close shave is an idiom for a narrow escape, when disaster was only just avoided.

clue.text: Antelope's caught by assistant putting down one lamb

indicators.note: the antelope word is caught inside the assistant word
in a down entry the one is moved lower, to the end of the assistant word

parts.note: an aide is an assistant
the Roman numeral for one is I
a gnu is an antelope; the 's gives the S

explanation.surface: An antelope trapped by a farmhand who has to put down a lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting down' reads literally in a down clue: the one is shifted lower in the word. 'lamb' looks like the animal being put down, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnus Dei is Latin for Lamb of God, a title for Christ and part of the Mass.

clue.text: Leaves novelist on track

parts.note: Graham Greene was an English novelist
RY, railway, is a railway track

explanation.surface: A novelist leaves while on the railway track, like a scene from a thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenery means green foliage, the leaves of plants collectively.

clue.text: Not still working around pine frame of espalier

indicators.note: the working word is turned around

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
to pine for something is to long for it

indicators.note: the outside letters of espalier, which frame the rest

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: A gardener's espalier, a tree trained flat on a frame, being worked around a pine.
explanation.definitionFit: No longer means not any more, the opposite of still in the sense of continuing.

clue.text: Funky reggae covers popular for displaying harmony

indicators.note: the rearranged letters cover, or surround, the popular word
funky suggests a loose, jumbled groove, so the letters of reggae are rearranged

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A band doing funky reggae cover versions of hits, all in harmony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' looks like cover versions of songs, but it is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are agreeing are in accord, showing harmony with one another.

clue.text: Rank or rating in this way given to instrument

indicators.note: the pieces are added to one another in sequence

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a naval rating
so means thus, in this way
a lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A question about whether a musician's standing or score comes from the instrument they play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' is the adjective, as in a rank amateur, not a noun for status.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank and absolute both mean complete or utter, as in a rank or absolute beginner.

clue.text: Talks about daughter and son's rapid search for mates

indicators.note: the talks word goes about, surrounding, the daughter letter

parts.note: speeches are formal talks
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone describing a daughter and son hurriedly hunting for partners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mates' means checkmates, not partners: speed chess is a fast form of the game in which each player hunts for checkmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed chess is played against a fast clock, so each player looks quickly for checkmate.

clue.text: Business price increases, dropping current merger

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business

indicators.note: the current letter is dropped from the price increases word

parts.note: inflation is a general rise in prices
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A company's rising prices fall back after it merges with another firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A conflation is a blending of two things into one, a fusion or combining.

clue.text: Radio's means of marketing woodcutter's tool

indicators.note: on radio words are heard, not seen, so the answer sounds like the word

parts.note: ads, advertisements, are a means of marketing

explanation.surface: A radio station's advertising pitch for a woodworking tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a cutting tool with an arched blade set at right angles to the handle, used for shaping timber.

clue.text: Foolish like figure saving face in imbroglio

indicators.note: the like and figure words keep, or save, the letter within them

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
nine is a figure, a number

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, its first letter

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: Someone acting foolishly, like a public figure trying to save face in a messy scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means extremely stupid, literally behaving like an ass.

clue.text: One that may fight complaint from a person wearing tiny pants

indicators.note: the person word goes inside the jumbled letters, as a body inside clothes
pants is slang for rubbish, so the letters of tiny are made a mess of

parts.note: bod is informal British for a person

explanation.surface: A grumble from someone squeezed into undersized underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' as a noun wants to be what the person wears; it is British slang for rubbish, the anagram signal. 'complaint' is an illness here.
explanation.definitionFit: Antibodies are proteins in the blood that combat infection, so they fight illness, a complaint.

clue.text: Fake mistreatment's covered I see

indicators.note: the mistreatment word covers, or surrounds, the other letters

parts.note: ill use is mistreatment; the 's means mistreatment has
V is short for vide, Latin for see, used in references

explanation.surface: A sham claim of mistreatment that has been hushed up, as a witness sees it.
explanation.definitionFit: Illusive means deceptive or illusory, so something illusive is unreal, a sham.

clue.text: Want this person to block unfortunate cut in income

indicators.note: the inner build goes inside the income word

parts.note: pay is income

indicators.note: the I goes inside to block the jumbled letters
unfortunate suggests things gone awry, so the letters of cut are jumbled

parts.note: this person is the setter, who is I

explanation.surface: The setter complaining about wanting to stop an unlucky pay cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this person' is the setter speaking, so it gives I. 'Want' is the noun meaning lack, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Paucity is scarcity or lack, so it is a noun for want in the sense of shortage.

clue.text: Heavyweight caught old American's boxing defeat

indicators.note: the first letters box, or enclose, the defeat word

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
US means American; the 's gives the letters as a possessive
a loss is a defeat

explanation.surface: A heavyweight boxer, an old American fighter, caught out and beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A colossus is something or someone of enormous size or importance, a giant.

clue.text: A French female saving time, at first, is unpleasant to listen to

indicators.note: the time letter is placed at the start

parts.note: une is the French feminine form of a
less means minus, except, as saving does in older usage

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman who keeps time but whose singing grates on the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' in the sense of except, as in 'saving your presence', matches less, as in 'less tax'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuneless sound has no melody, so it is grating and unmusical to hear.

clue.text: Fan jacket of denim, drier on the outside

indicators.note: the drier word goes on the outside of the denim letters

parts.note: an airer is a clothes drier

indicators.note: the jacket of a word is its outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: A denim jacket hung on a clothes airer to dry.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is a devoted follower or enthusiast, which is what a fan is.

clue.text: Charge directed at liberals

parts.note: to means towards, directed at
L is the abbreviation for Liberal; doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A fee aimed squarely at Liberal politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A toll is a fee, for instance to use a road or bridge.

clue.text: Brief note on account book showing addition to staff

indicators.note: the note word comes after, sitting on, the account book word

parts.note: a ledger is a book of accounts
a line is a short letter, as in drop me a line

explanation.surface: A short memo written in the company accounts to record that a new employee has joined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' is the musical stave, not employees.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledger line is a short line added above or below the musical stave for notes outside its range.

clue.text: Sweet treats one fed to black dog with no tail

indicators.note: the pieces are joined in sequence

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: the last letter, the tail, is removed from the dog word

parts.note: a Scottie is a Scottish terrier

clue.text: Asian city's market lacking nothing

indicators.note: the nothing letter is missing from the market word

parts.note: an agora was a marketplace in ancient Greece
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.definitionFit: Agra is a city in northern India, famous as the site of the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Maybe roll cook tries after something on a plate

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come after

parts.note: REG, registration, is shown on a British car's number plate

indicators.note: to cook the books is to fiddle them, so the letters of tries are rearranged

clue.text: American's dropped ecstasy round bed where fliers might sleep

explanation.definitionFit: A dovecote is a shelter where doves or pigeons roost.

clue.text: Take another look at queen with spinning jenny?

indicators.note: the queen letters are spun round

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for queen
a jenny is a female donkey; cryptically an ass-ess, as in lioness, with the question mark flagging the made-up word

explanation.surface: A queen working with a spinning jenny, the early machine for spinning cotton.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface splits the phrase spinning jenny: 'spinning' acts on the queen and 'jenny?' is a female ass, playfully an ASS with the feminine ending ESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassess is to evaluate again, so it means reconsidering or reviewing something.
